what: S2-02 adjudication: the v1>=v2 ordering claim (03_method.tex:62) is proved only for the UNSTRATIFIED mixture bound, while the estimator is stratified within n_opt.
verified_by: MAIN, 2026-08-15, 0 GPU. Per-stratum gold marginals read from the 8 per-item shards of 7B_base on zwfy6 (.73); shard set == {0..7}, n=12032, 0 dup, 0 nan.

algebra.what_stratification_gives: acc_hat <= sum_s w_s max_L m_(s,L)   [per-stratum argmax]
algebra.why_that_is_weaker: max_L sum_s w_s m_(s,L) <= sum_s w_s max_L m_(s,L); the ordering is recovered IFF argmax_L m_(s,L) is the same letter in every stratum
algebra.reviewer_counterexample_reproduced: 2 strata, w=(.5,.5), gold all-A in one and all-B in the other: f_const=0.5 but acc_hat=1.0, so acc_hat>f_const

verdict: The 'always' is FALSE as a theorem: argmax_L differs from the global best letter in 4 of 8 n_opt strata (n_opt=5,6,7,8). The ordering nevertheless HOLDS in 27/27 measured cells, but the tightest cell clears the floor by 0.0078 pp while the unproven region is 0.2992 pp wide -- 38x the observed margin. So the claim must be restated as an empirical property of these cells with its margin reported, not asserted as an identity.
